_about: Malady Wise famous non-health days (culture, festivals, religious and UN international days), shown ONLY on the /days/ calendar and list (days/days.js and _scripts/build_days.py). NOT read by the home page or puzzle builders, and NEVER used as puzzle themes. Same fields as data/health-days.json. tags: culture (all), religious (faith festivals: respectful, no jokes), au (Australian visitors only). rule 'dates' = moveable (lunar, lunisolar or church calendar): the dates map is authoritative, verified per year, and must be added by hand for new years (see _note for sources). After editing, run python3 _scripts/build_days.py.

days.name: New Year's Day
days.blurb: The first day of the Gregorian calendar year, and a public holiday in most countries.

days.name: Orthodox Christmas
days.blurb: Christmas for Orthodox churches that keep the Julian calendar, now 13 days behind the Gregorian one.

days.name: International Holocaust Remembrance Day
days.blurb: The UN day remembering the six million Jews and millions of others murdered in the Holocaust, on the anniversary of the liberation of Auschwitz-Birkenau in 1945.

days.name: Lunar New Year
days.blurb: New Year on the Chinese lunisolar calendar, celebrated across East and South-East Asia and worldwide. 2026 is the Year of the Horse; 2027 the Year of the Goat.
days._note: Moveable (Chinese lunisolar calendar). Checked: Farmers' Almanac, publicholidays sites.

days.name: Black History Month: US and Canada
days.blurb: February celebrates the history, achievements and culture of Black Americans and Black Canadians.

days.name: Valentine's Day
days.blurb: Cards, flowers and chocolates for loved ones, named after St Valentine.

days.name: Shrove Tuesday (Mardi Gras, Pancake Day)
days.blurb: The day before Lent begins: pancakes in the UK and Australia, carnival in New Orleans and Rio. It falls 47 days before Easter Sunday.

days.name: Ramadan
days.blurb: The Islamic month of fasting from dawn to sunset, prayer and charity. Dates follow the Islamic lunar calendar and moon sighting, so they can differ by a day between countries.
days._note: Moveable (Islamic calendar). 2026 actual; 2027 expected (Gulf News, astronomical calculation).

days.name: Holi
days.blurb: The Hindu festival of colours, welcoming spring with bonfires the night before and coloured powder on the day. Some regions mark it a day earlier.
days._note: Moveable (Hindu lunisolar calendar). Checked: officeholidays.com (2026: 4 Mar in most states, 3 Mar in some; 2027: 22 Mar).

days.name: Eid al-Fitr
days.blurb: The festival that ends Ramadan, with prayers, family feasts and gifts. Dates follow the Islamic lunar calendar and moon sighting, so they can differ by a day between countries.
days._note: Moveable. 2026 actual; 2027 expected 9 or 10 March (Gulf News).

days.name: Nowruz (Persian New Year)
days.blurb: New Year at the spring equinox, celebrated in Iran, Central Asia, the Caucasus and beyond. The UN marks it on 21 March.

days.name: Passover (Pesach)
days.blurb: The Jewish festival remembering the Exodus from Egypt, starting with the Seder meal at sundown the evening before.

days.name: Easter Sunday
days.blurb: The main Christian festival, celebrating the resurrection of Jesus. Its date moves with the spring full moon.

days.name: Orthodox Easter
days.blurb: Easter for Orthodox churches, calculated on the Julian calendar, so it often falls later than Western Easter.

days.name: Songkran (Thai New Year)
days.blurb: Thailand's New Year, famous for the nationwide water fight. Similar water festivals happen in Laos, Myanmar and Cambodia.

days.name: World Press Freedom Day
days.blurb: The UN day for a free and independent press.

days.name: Mother's Day
days.blurb: Second Sunday of May in Australia, the US, Canada and many other countries. The UK and Ireland mark Mothering Sunday in Lent.

days.name: Eid al-Adha
days.blurb: The Festival of Sacrifice, at the time of the Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca. Dates follow the Islamic lunar calendar and moon sighting, so they can differ by a day between countries.
days._note: Moveable. 2026 actual; 2027 expected (Gulf News: Arafat Day 15 May).

days.name: Pride Month
days.blurb: June celebrates LGBTIQA+ communities, marking the 1969 Stonewall uprising in New York. Sydney's Mardi Gras is in February.

days.name: Juneteenth
days.blurb: A US federal holiday marking the end of slavery, when news of emancipation reached Galveston, Texas, on 19 June 1865.

days.name: Father's Day
days.blurb: Third Sunday of June in the US, UK, Canada and many other countries. Australia and New Zealand mark it in September.

days.name: Father's Day (Australia)
days.blurb: First Sunday of September in Australia and New Zealand.

days.name: Rosh Hashanah
days.blurb: The Jewish New Year, with the shofar (ram's horn) and apples dipped in honey. It begins at sundown the evening before.

days.name: Yom Kippur
days.blurb: The Day of Atonement, the holiest day of the Jewish year, marked by a 25-hour fast. It begins at sundown the evening before.

days.name: Mid-Autumn Festival
days.blurb: The harvest moon festival of mooncakes and lanterns, on the 15th day of the eighth lunar month.

days.name: Black History Month: UK and Ireland
days.blurb: October celebrates the history, achievements and contributions of Black people in Britain and Ireland.

days.name: United Nations Day
days.blurb: The anniversary of the UN Charter coming into force in 1945.

days.name: Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead)
days.blurb: Mexico's joyful remembrance of loved ones who have died, with ofrendas (altars), marigolds and sugar skulls.

days.name: Guy Fawkes Night (Bonfire Night)
days.blurb: Bonfires and fireworks across Britain, marking the failed Gunpowder Plot of 1605.

days.name: Diwali
days.blurb: The festival of lights, celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs and Jains with lamps, fireworks and sweets. The festival runs over about five days.
days._note: Moveable (Hindu lunisolar calendar). Checked: publicholidays.co.uk (Sun 8 Nov 2026, Fri 29 Oct 2027).

days.name: International Day for Tolerance
days.blurb: The UN day for respect and understanding between cultures, faiths and peoples.

days.name: World Children's Day
days.blurb: UNICEF's day for children's rights, on the anniversary of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989).

days.name: US Thanksgiving
days.blurb: Turkey, family and football in the United States on the fourth Thursday of November. Canada's Thanksgiving is in October.

days.name: Hanukkah
days.blurb: The Jewish festival of lights: eight nights of candles on the menorah, starting at sundown on the first date.
days._note: Moveable (Hebrew calendar). Checked: Hebcal (first candle 4/12/2026 and 24/12/2027).

days.name: Human Rights Day
days.blurb: The anniversary of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by the UN in 1948.

days.name: Christmas Day
days.blurb: The Christian festival celebrating the birth of Jesus, and a public holiday in many countries.
